content: Carrier oils, also referred to as base oils or vegetable oils, are utilized to dilute essential oils and absolutes before they are applied to the skin. These oils are termed carrier oils because they serve as a medium to carry the essential oils onto the skin. Unlike essential oils, carrier oils do not possess a concentrated aroma and do not evaporate in the same manner. There exists a wide variety of carrier oils, each with unique properties and specific suitability for different treatments in aromatherapy. Infused oils are a blend of a carrier oil and various herbs, enhancing their therapeutic potential. True carrier oils are typically cold-pressed vegetable oils. Examples of such oils include sweet almond oil, grapeseed oil, avocado oil, olive oil, sesame oil, evening primrose oil, sunflower oil, jojoba oil, and emu oil. Additionally, oils derived from nuts, such as walnut oil, peanut oil, pecan oil, and macadamia nut oil, as well as fractionated coconut oil, are also considered carrier oils. Among these, sweet almond oil and grapeseed oil are the most commonly used carrier oils due to their versatility and compatibility with a wide range of applications.
